response.sql: WITH c AS (SELECT p.bats AS bats, COUNT(*) AS n FROM appearances a JOIN player p ON a.player_id = p.player_id WHERE p.bats <> '' GROUP BY p.bats) SELECT bats, n AS appearance_count, n * 1.0 / SUM(n) OVER () AS fraction_of_total, n * 1.0 / AVG(n * 1.0) OVER () AS ratio_to_avg_group_count FROM c

assumptions.assumption: Players with a NULL bats value are excluded along with empty-string ones, because `bats <> ''` is not true for NULL. The request only mentions empty strings, so a NULL group could arguably be kept.
player_id is unique in player, so the inner join does not duplicate appearance records.
The average count per batting-hand group is the mean of the group counts over the retained groups, so the last column is count divided by that mean.

alternatives.interpretation: Keep players whose bats is NULL as their own group, and exclude only the empty-string value.
alternatives.sql: WITH c AS (SELECT p.bats AS bats, COUNT(*) AS n FROM appearances a JOIN player p ON a.player_id = p.player_id WHERE p.bats IS NULL OR p.bats <> '' GROUP BY p.bats) SELECT bats, n AS appearance_count, n * 1.0 / SUM(n) OVER () AS fraction_of_total, n * 1.0 / AVG(n * 1.0) OVER () AS ratio_to_avg_group_count FROM c
